title: Rob Reiner wins posthumous Emmy for role in series The Bear
seoTitle: Rob Reiner wins posthumous Emmy for role in The Bear
subtitle: Actor and filmmaker was awarded in the best guest actor in a comedy series category during the Creative Arts Emmy Awards.
excerpt: Rob Reiner received a posthumous Emmy for best guest actor in a comedy series for his performance in the fourth season of The Bear.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Folha de S.Paulo, Portal iG, SAPO
contentHtml:
Rob Reiner was honored with a posthumous Emmy in the best guest actor in a comedy series category for his performance in the fourth season of the series The Bear. The winner announcement took place during the Creative Arts Emmy Awards, an event that precedes the main ceremony and includes technical and special‑participation trophies.

The posthumous win in The Bear

In the production, the artist portrayed a businessman who decides to help one of the employees at the restaurant run by Jeremy Allen White's character. Reiner's performance in the ninth episode of the fourth season, titled "Tonnato," secured the trophy after beating the other nominees in the category.

A history of awards and career

This recognition adds to two earlier victories the artist achieved in his television career. Rob Reiner had previously won in 1974 and 1978 for his work on the sitcom *All in the Family*. Beyond acting, he built a directing career with films such as *Stand by Me*, *This Is Spinal Tap*, *The Princess Bride* and the romantic comedy *When Harry Met Sally*.

The standing ovation at the ceremony

During the event, the audience gave a standing ovation lasting about a minute after the posthumous win was announced. Host Wendi McLendon‑Covey asked the crowd to rise before revealing the winner, creating an emotional moment as they recalled the legacy of the late actor and filmmaker.

The competitors in the category

To claim the best guest actor in a comedy series award, Reiner competed against other television names. Nominees included Michael J. Fox and Brett Goldstein for *Real Talk*, Christopher McDonald for *Hacks*, Hamish Linklater for *The Secret of Widow's Bay* and Connor Storrie for *Saturday Night Live*.
